text: Our dad died and left the house in his will. My sister A wants to buy it with her husband at a "family discount". I'm not signing off on that. Our younger sister B could use some money too. Can you help us sort this out?

I'm sorry about your father. Yes, I can help the three of you talk this through. I can't make legal decisions or move money, but I can help you find a plan you all accept.

I will keep a short list of each person's concerns, which I call NCEs. Here is what I have from you so far. Please correct anything I got wrong.

NCE 1 (C): You do not agree to A buying the house at a "family discount."
NCE 2 (C): You want B's need for money to be taken into account.

Could you tell me more? What would a fair price look like to you? What does the will say about how the house is split? Is there anything else that matters to you, such as timing or keeping the house in the family?

Those NCEs are mostly right: I want a fair financial share, and I won’t subsidize A’s discounted purchase. I can’t speak for B’s needs. I don’t know what the will says, and no price or split is settled. I’d want an independent valuation to help set a fair price. I’d like this resolved, but there’s no rush.

I'm sorry about your father. C asked me to help the three of you work out a plan for his house. I can't make legal decisions or move money. I can help you talk it through and keep track of what matters to each of you.

I keep a list of each person's concerns, which I call NCEs. I would like to add yours. I understand you and your husband may want to buy the house. What matters most to you here? What price or terms would you see as fair, and why? Is there anything about timing, the will, or the house itself I should know?

Thank you. My husband and I would like to buy the house, ideally at a family discount. I want financial independence, and owning it would help with that. I don’t know what price or terms would be fair yet, and I can’t proceed without C’s agreement. I’m not sure about the timing or legal details.

I'm sorry about your father. C asked me to help the three of you work out a plan for his house. I can't make legal decisions or move money. I can help you talk it through and keep track of what matters to each of you.

I keep a list of each person's concerns, which I call NCEs. I would like to add yours in your own words. What matters most to you about the house and the will? Is there anything about money, timing, or the house itself that you want the others to understand?
Thank you. I’d like the will and house plan to leave me with some money to start a dance studio. I don’t know what’s fair yet, but I hope we can keep that in mind as we talk it through.

Thank you, A. Here is the full list of concerns so far. Please tell me if I got yours wrong or missed anything.

NCE 1 (A): You and your husband would like to buy the house, ideally at a family discount. Owning it would help your financial independence.
NCE 2 (C): C wants a fair financial share and will not subsidize a discounted purchase.
NCE 3 (C): C would like an independent valuation to help set a price. C wants this resolved, but there is no rush.
NCE 4 (B): B hopes the plan leaves her some money to start a dance studio.
NCE 5 (mine): No one yet knows what the will says. I think the first step is for all three of you to read it and, if needed, get advice from the executor or a lawyer. Any plan should fit the will.

NCE 1 and NCE 2 pull against each other. One idea to test: get an independent valuation, then A buys at that price, and B and C receive their shares in cash. A "discount" could come only from a sister who freely chooses to give one. Would that work for you? If not, please say so. My suggestion is only a starting point.

The list is right. That plan wouldn’t work for me as stated: I’m hoping for a family discount, not necessarily to buy at the full valuation. I don’t know what price is fair yet, and it would also need C’s agreement.

Thank you, B. Here is the full list of concerns so far. Please tell me if I got yours wrong or missed anything.

NCE 1 (A): A and her husband would like to buy the house, ideally at a family discount. Owning it would help her financial independence.
NCE 2 (C): C wants a fair financial share and will not subsidize a discounted purchase.
NCE 3 (C): C would like an independent valuation to help set a price. C wants this resolved, but there is no rush.
NCE 4 (B): You hope the plan leaves you some money to start a dance studio.
NCE 5 (mine): No one yet knows what the will says. All three of you should read it and, if needed, get advice from the executor or a lawyer.

One idea to test: get an independent valuation, then A buys at that price, and you and C receive your shares in cash. That could give you money toward the studio. Would that work for you? Do you have a sense of timing, for example when you would need the money? Please disagree if this does not fit.

An independent valuation sounds sensible, and cash toward the studio would help. I’m not sure the plan works until we know what the will says and what each of our shares would be. I don’t have a firm timing in mind yet.

Thank you, C. Here is where things stand.

NCE 1 (A): A and her husband would like to buy the house, ideally at a family discount. Owning it would help her financial independence.
NCE 2 (C): You want a fair financial share and will not subsidize a discounted purchase.
NCE 3 (C): You want an independent valuation to help set a price. There is no rush.
NCE 4 (B): B hopes for some money to start a dance studio. She has no firm timing.
NCE 5 (mine): No one yet knows what the will says. You three should read it first, with the executor or a lawyer if needed.

A has said full valuation does not work for her as stated. B agrees with a valuation but wants to see the will first.

Here is a middle path to test. The price stays at the independent valuation, so your share is not reduced. Because you said there is no rush, you could offer A a different kind of help, such as more time to pay or payment in stages. That might help A afford it without cutting what you receive. Would you consider something like that? If not, please say so plainly.
I’d consider discussing staged payment, but not a discount or terms that put my share at risk. Let’s read the will first; I’m not agreeing to anything yet.

Thank you, A. I have added your view to NCE 1: full valuation does not work for you as stated.

C has said she will not agree to a discount or to terms that put her share at risk. She is willing to discuss paying in stages. She also wants to read the will before agreeing to anything.

So here is a question for you. If the price matched the valuation, but you could pay B and C over time, would that help you enough? If not, what is it about the price that matters most to you, for example the total cost, the size of a mortgage, or something else? Knowing this may help us find other options. B and C have not agreed to anything yet.

Paying in stages could help with the cash flow, but a full valuation still may be more than I can manage. The total cost matters most; I can’t commit without knowing the valuation and reading the will.

Thank you, A. All three of you agree on the next two steps, so I am sending the same summary to everyone.

Agreed next steps:
1. All three of you read the will together, with the executor or a lawyer if needed, to learn each share.
2. You get one independent valuation of the house, with all three of you agreeing on who does it.

Open points to revisit after that:
- A says total cost matters most, and full valuation may be more than she can manage. Paying in stages could help.
- C will discuss paying in stages, but not a discount or terms that put her share at risk.
- B hopes for cash toward a dance studio and wants to see the shares first.
- If A cannot afford the house at valuation, other options include selling it and splitting the money, or one sister choosing freely to give part of her own share.

No one has agreed to a price or plan. Please tell me if this summary is wrong.
That summary is right. I haven’t agreed to a price or plan.

No one has agreed to a price or plan. Please tell me if this summary is wrong.
That summary sounds right. Paying in stages could delay money for the studio, so I’d want to understand the timing and make sure my share is protected before agreeing to anything.

Thank you, C. A and B have both confirmed this summary, and I would like your confirmation too.

Agreed next steps:
1. All three of you read the will together, with the executor or a lawyer if needed, to learn each share.
2. You get one independent valuation of the house, with all three of you agreeing on who does it.

- You will discuss paying in stages, but not a discount or terms that put your share at risk.
- B hopes for cash toward a dance studio. She is worried that paying in stages could delay her money, and she wants her share protected.
- If A cannot afford the house at valuation, other options include selling it and splitting the money, or one sister choosing freely to give part of her own share.

No one has agreed to a price or plan. Please tell me if anything is wrong.
That’s right. I’m willing to discuss staged payments after we’ve read the will and agreed on an independent valuation, but I haven’t agreed to a plan.
